clue.text: Are apt to look like nurse

definitions.meaning: to be inclined or likely to do something
to look after or care for someone

explanation.surface: Someone tends to resemble a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look like' is only a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The one verb covers both an inclination (people tend to grumble) and caring for a patient (tending the sick).

clue.text: Writings about one young lady

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the writings go round the single letter

parts.note: MSS is the abbreviation for manuscripts, i.e. writings
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Letters written concerning a single girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The title used for an unmarried girl or young woman, so the word stands for her.

clue.text: That is to say about 500 left doing nothing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the abbreviation goes round the other two letters

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is to say
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Roughly five hundred people were left sitting around with nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inactive or unoccupied is a plain synonym for lazing about.

clue.text: Second man fitting in the chief officer

indicators.note: in places the word for fitting inside the biblical name

parts.note: Cain, son of Adam, was the second man on earth after his father
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A deputy is being measured for the head officer's uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second man' looks like a deputy, but it is a biblical riddle: after Adam, his son Cain was the second man.
explanation.definitionFit: The commander of a ship or team is its senior officer.

clue.text: The consequence when I'm left with broken cane

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
port is the nautical term for the left side of a ship

indicators.note: broken means the letters of cane are smashed and put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on what happens when they are left holding a snapped cane.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequence in the old sense of weight or significance, as in a person of consequence.

clue.text: Where one should yawn when late

definitions.meaning: politely, one yawns behind one's hand

explanation.surface: A lesson in manners for when someone arrives late.
explanation.definitionFit: Good manners put a yawn behind the hand, and the compound means behind schedule or in arrears.

clue.text: Leaves off at intervals

parts.note: reads as stopping now and then, but describes trees whose leaves come off seasonally

explanation.definitionFit: Trees of this kind shed their foliage each autumn, at regular intervals.

clue.text: A few like this with me

parts.note: so means in this way, like this

explanation.surface: Someone says a few people share their opinion, like them.
explanation.definitionFit: An unspecified small number, as in some people agree.

clue.text: Hothead sees potential storm boil over

indicators.note: potential suggests something that could become something else, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered person watches a possible storm come to the boil.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian island volcano Stromboli is the hothead; 'over' only adds to the boiling picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano has a fiery top, so it is jokily called a hothead.

clue.text: Boy shortly returned with energy and a twitch, suffering from indigestion

indicators.note: returned means the short name is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: Syd is a shortened form of the boy's name Sydney
pep means vigour or energy
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A young lad comes back full of beans and twitching, with a bad stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is the medical word for indigestion, so this adjective describes someone afflicted by it.

clue.text: Friend having most of the stake

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped from the word for a stake

parts.note: a pale is a pointed wooden stake, as in a fence

explanation.surface: A friend holds the larger share of the money bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stake' suggests a wager, but it is a fence post, PALE, losing its E.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for a mate or chum.

clue.text: Scope for ducks in the Marines

indicators.note: in places the two round letters inside the abbreviation

parts.note: RM stands for the Royal Marines
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, written as the letter O, so two ducks give two of them

explanation.surface: There is space for waterfowl among the soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, so each duck is an O.
explanation.definitionFit: Room for manoeuvre means scope or latitude.

clue.text: The first person to perform in an international language

parts.note: I is the first person singular pronoun
to do is to perform or carry out

explanation.surface: Someone is the first to perform in a foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ido is an artificial auxiliary language derived from Esperanto, meant for worldwide use.

clue.text: Fit to do the job with reservations

definitions.meaning: having the right credentials or training
restricted or hedged, as of praise or approval

explanation.surface: A candidate is passed as competent, but only grudgingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained person holds the certificates for a post, while limited agreement is hedged with conditions.

clue.text: Child of four telephoned the French square

parts.note: a quad is a quadruplet, one of four children born together
rang means called on the phone
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A four-year-old phoned a square in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Child of four' looks like a four-year-old, but it is one of quadruplets.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtyard enclosed by buildings, as at a college, is a four-sided open space.

clue.text: Blows against business

definitions.note: plural verb in the surface but read as a noun for the wind

parts.note: anti means opposed to or against
trade means commerce or business

explanation.surface: Strikes are aimed against commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: The antitrades are winds blowing above and opposite the trade winds.

clue.text: In it a mean arrangement that lacks any sign of life

definitions.text: that lacks any sign of life

indicators.note: arrangement means the letters of these words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A stingy layout leaves something looking lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless or not alive, like a stone or a table.

clue.text: Mum has no hesitation swatting it

definitions.text: Mum has no hesitation swatting it

indicators.note: has no means the hesitation sound is removed from the word for mum

parts.note: mother is a fuller word for mum
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A mother swats a winged pest without thinking twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: the insect is what mum swats without a second thought.
explanation.definitionFit: The fluttering insect that eats clothes is the one a mother swats unhesitatingly.

clue.text: Favourite piece, one by a novice

parts.note: a part is a piece of something
I is the Roman numeral for one
L for learner, as on learner drivers' plates

explanation.surface: A preferred section was performed by a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fond of something or biased towards it, as in partial to a drink.

clue.text: In Lancashire town, go back to the city

indicators.note: in puts the reversed word inside the town's name

parts.note: Colne is a town in Lancashire, northern England

indicators.note: back means the word go is read backwards

explanation.surface: A Lancashire resident is told to return to the city.
explanation.walkthrough: Colne is a mill town in Lancashire, a county of north-west England; 'back' makes OG.
explanation.definitionFit: A major German city on the Rhine, famous for its cathedral and eau de toilette.

clue.text: Expelled from an aeroplane seat perhaps

definitions.meaning: shot out of a cockpit by an ejector seat

explanation.surface: A pilot is thrown out of a plane by the ejector seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown out of a club or a pub, and fired clear of a jet by a pilot's escape seat.

clue.text: Wrong to return at a steady pace

indicators.note: return means the legal word for a wrong is read backwards

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: It is wrong to go back at an even speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A jogging gait, a pace between walking and running.

clue.text: Unfairness of being in only very cold water

parts.note: just means merely or only
ice is water cold enough to freeze

explanation.surface: Something unfair about being made to swim in freezing water.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrong done to someone, a lack of fairness or justice.

clue.text: As well as the first fifteen letters of the alphabet

parts.words: the first fifteen letters of the alphabet
parts.note: the opening fifteen letters are written as a range from the first letter to the last, and the tail of that range gives the reading

explanation.surface: Someone recites the first fifteen letters of the alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' links. The fifteen letters run from A through O, said as 'A to O', and the last two words of that, to O, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Also or in addition, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Strange sort of punch

definitions.meaning: odd or peculiar, in old British slang
a spirit used in mixed drinks like punch

explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for odd or peculiar, and the spirit from sugar cane used in a punch bowl.

clue.text: Girl who does not know whether she is coming or going

indicators.text: who does not know whether she is coming or going
indicators.note: a name reading the same forwards and backwards cannot tell which way it is travelling

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A muddled young woman is completely confused.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female given name, and a palindrome that reads identically in either direction, so it seems unsure of its heading.

clue.text: Sold the lot

parts.note: seems to mean selling everything, but a lot is an item put up for bidding

explanation.definitionFit: Sale by bidding, where each item is a lot knocked down to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Traditionally included a detached area

indicators.note: included means the letters are held within the word

explanation.surface: A remote spot was traditionally part of the arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is an island off western Scotland, land cut off by water.

clue.text: Note a word of hesitation inside will shock

indicators.note: inside places the hesitation word within the abbreviation

parts.note: NB stands for nota bene, note well
um is a sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: A written reminder with an awkward pause will come as a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun or deaden feeling, as a shock does.

clue.text: Pulled and tied

explanation.surface: A team was pulled level and the match was tied.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of a verb meaning to haul, and a sporting result with level scores.

clue.text: Sole variety of fruit

indicators.note: variety of means a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of flatfish is offered as fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like the fish, but it is only the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The small bitter blackthorn berry, used in sloe gin.

clue.text: Two will go into feeling still less sensation

parts.note: even as in even more, still more
more numb means having less sensation

explanation.surface: Two people are going into a state with still less feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Any figure divisible by 2 without remainder.
